work.permit: Prior written permission of an authorised officer

note: Majority: the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, article 260 (read from the Kenya Law Reform Commission's text): an adult is an individual who has attained eighteen, and a child one who hasn't; held as the age of majority. The Age of Majority Act (Cap. 33) itself wasn't read: Kenya Law (new.kenyalaw.org) answered with an AWS WAF challenge, not passed, and archive.org dropped every connection on 2026-10-31. Work: the Employment (General) Rules, 2014 (subsidiary legislation under the Employment Act, 2007, read from the State Department for Labour's scanned copy), rule 12: no one may employ a child under sixteen without the prior written permission of an authorised officer, renewed yearly; a child of thirteen to sixteen may be employed only in the light work of the Fifth Schedule or as an apprentice; and no child may work in a bar, hotel, restaurant or club selling liquor. The Act's own section 56, which bars employing a child under thirteen, wasn't read in an official copy. Performers: the Rules name no rule for a performer, so a performer under sixteen is held to the same permit from thirteen, and none under thirteen: a reading; whether the Fifth Schedule's light work includes performing wasn't read (the schedule's scan has no text). Service: none. The Government of Kenya's declaration on its ratification of the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on armed conflict (read from Bayefsky's copy of the UN treaty record): the minimum age for recruitment into the armed forces is by law eighteen, recruitment is entirely voluntary, and there is no conscription in Kenya. The Kenya Defence Forces Act, 2012, itself wasn't read.

sources.title: Bayefsky (UN human rights treaties): Kenya, CRC Optional Protocol (Armed Conflict), reservations and declarations
sources.said: The Government of the Republic of Kenya declares that the minimum age for the recruitment of persons into the armed forces is by law set at eighteen years. Recruitment is entirely and genuinely voluntary and is carried out with the full informed consent of the persons being recruited. There is no conscription in Kenya.
